reply_text:
🈹 ("the cascade should be constructed not chosen") You are right, and "chosen" was wrong for what the machine does as well as for what it should do. I take the word back, and with it the third step I proposed earlier, which treated the graph as a source of ready-made cascades to pick among. The graph prior belongs inside construction.

㊢ (what the click does today) I read the construction code (`interpretation_construction.clj`):
- **The cascade is constructed.** The code searches backward from the mission's wants, adding a pattern wherever one produces a want or something another pattern needs, and then orders the result by need. The last click's record marks its cascade "machine-constructed".
- **Only the per-want pattern is chosen.** A seat names one library pattern for each want, and those readings are the material the construction searches over.
- **Construction already has a place for a prior.** It ranks its proposals with a prior, and that prior is currently computed from the separate feedback file.
- **Construction can only use patterns that have a reading for the mission.** A reading says what the pattern needs and what it produces there. The graph's connecting patterns, such as `test-registry/register-the-run`, have no such reading, so the search cannot use them today.

㊭ (where the giant cascade enters construction) Two places, in this order:
1. **Ranking of proposals.** Replace the feedback-file prior with one computed from the graph, so that a proposal whose patterns are linked in the giant cascade ranks ahead of one whose patterns are not. This also removes one of the two readers of the feedback file.
2. **The material.** When construction has its patterns, the graph's neighbours and connecting patterns are put forward for a reading against the mission. The ones that get a reading join the search.

Step 2 changes what work a click does, so I would size it separately after step 1.

㊢ (wording fixed) The view's code and one test name said "chosen"; they now say "constructed cascade" (futon2 `0dd9507a1`, reloaded). The view itself is unchanged: it reads the constructed cascade's patterns and takes no part in building it.

🈸 (two decisions)
1. Shall I have step 1 written now? I would first have the graph prior specified as a formula you can read, since the present one has no theory source.
2. The click request from my last report still stands. It would show a constructed cascade against the graph before any of this changes.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the example diff) It is in `futon2/test/fixtures/pattern-graph-diff/2026-10-05-c9d25d6a.expected-diff.json` (futon2 `9cf58ebfc`). It has three parts:
- **Source:** the run, its mission, that the run failed at the reviewer check, that the selected cascade was the one carried out, and the futon7 commit it produced.
- **Four uses:** one per pattern, with its position in the cascade, the want it was chosen for, and that want's outcome. For this run every outcome is "not-recorded", because the want accounting failed in that run. From the next click on these will read reached, progressed, blocked or untouched.
- **Six links of a new kind, "used-together":** one per pair of patterns in the cascade, each with the run and the order the two were applied in.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what applying it would change) I computed this without applying it:
- **Five of the six pairs have no link in the graph today.** The sixth, `orchestration/recorded-handoff` with `measurement/warrant-travels-with-the-number`, has one "next-in-session" link.
- **`ukrns/reader-run-path` would join the connected part**, which grows from 734 to 735 patterns.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
("use that as a prior to help us construct a small local cascade") Two findings bear on this:
- **How the click forms its cascade today:** for each want, a seat is asked to name one library pattern that produces it, and the four answers are then put in order. The graph is not read at any point, which is why the four patterns of the last click are mostly unlinked in it.
- **What already exists:** on 30 September a set of futon2 modules was written that takes a few seed patterns and finds the smallest connected piece of the graph containing them. That is a local cascade cut out of the giant one. They have tests, and the click runner does not call them.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(in flight) Two jobs, both parked:
- **codex-10, diff producer:** a function that turns a run's facts into this diff, tested against the example file. It is not wired into the click and applies nothing. Job `invoke-1791185301323-32711-ac6930f4`, park `park-d5a052d9-4084-4bba-b5ac-40f2d9620cee`.
- **codex-12, read-only discovery:** where each want gets its pattern and where a prior from the graph could enter; whether the 30 September modules have the inputs they need for the last click's mission; what they return for its four patterns; and whether any note says why they were left unconnected. Job `invoke-1791185304798-32712-24dac2cd`, park `park-6c81a4f0-08f6-4b5b-96df-6c22f2dc70b3`.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(next, after those return)
1. An inspect-and-apply tool beside the graph generator. It shows what a diff would change, as above, and applies it only on your say. The generator would read applied diffs as one more source, so that rebuilding the graph keeps them.
2. A first step that makes cascade construction read the graph, sized after codex-12's answers.
